Quotation guidance:

---
# Quoting speech

Read this before putting quotation marks around anything somebody said. It applies to interview transcripts, recorded remarks, meeting notes, and any other material where the words are a person's rather than a document's.

Speech is not written prose, and a transcript quoted raw reads as carelessness towards the speaker rather than fidelity to them. So a spoken quotation may be repaired — cautiously, within a boundary that is easier to state than to feel your way to.

When translating permitted quotations, preserve meaning, stance, certainty and distinctive voice in idiomatic target-language speech, not source-language syntax. The restrictions below protect that substance; they do not require word-for-word translation. Make an implicit referent explicit only when the supplied context settles it. Where the meaning remains ambiguous, paraphrase what is established rather than inventing a fluent interpretation.

## What may be repaired

The syntax of speech: a sentence abandoned halfway and restarted, a subject left behind by its verb, a clause that never closes. Fillers — *you know*, *sort of*, *liksom*, *alltså* — where they carry nothing. Repetition that is the speaker searching for a word rather than insisting on one. False starts, and the small disfluencies a person does not hear themselves make.

That is the whole list. Everything on it is noise the speaker did not intend to produce, and removing it leaves what they meant to say.

## What may not

**Meaning.** Not narrowed, not widened, not sharpened. A speaker who said *most of them* has not said *all of them*, and one who said *we looked at it* has not said *we rejected it*.

**Stance.** Approval stays approval, reluctance stays reluctance, and a speaker who was careful not to blame anybody is not made to blame somebody by a tidier sentence.

**Certainty.** *I think*, *probably*, *as far as I know*, and *we are not sure yet* are the claim, not padding on it. Removing a hedge manufactures a confidence the speaker did not have; adding one takes away a confidence they did.

**Distinctive wording.** Where the speaker reached for an unusual word, an image, a piece of slang, or a phrasing that is theirs, it stays. Smoothing it into the register of the surrounding article is the most tempting of these failures and the one a reader can least detect.

**A self-correction.** Where a speaker gives a number or a fact and then corrects it, the correction is what they said. Quoting the first version is a misquotation; quoting a version that never existed — the correction with the correcting away — is worse.

**Anything additive.** Add no new meaning: no fact, stance, certainty, name, figure or connection that the speaker did not supply. A permitted repair or translation may change words only to render that same meaning.

## When to paraphrase instead

Where fidelity is uncertain, paraphrase. A paraphrase that attributes carefully — *she said the change had taken about a year, and that she was not sure it would hold* — is accurate, useful, and honest about what the material supports. A fluent direct quotation assembled out of a fragmentary answer is none of those things, however good it sounds.

The cases that should turn into paraphrase: material that is a summary of what somebody said rather than their words; a transcript too broken to repair inside the boundary above; several remarks that would have to be welded together to make one sentence; and any moment where you find yourself choosing between two readings of what the speaker meant.

Signal what the material actually is. Where the source is notes rather than a recording, the text says what the person said and does not pretend to their exact wording.

## What stays outside this

Whether the speaker approves the quotation. Quote approval is a human arrangement between the writer and the person quoted, and nothing here verifies it or stands in for it. A draft may say a quotation is unapproved; it may not treat the absence of approval as a problem it has solved.
---

Swedish composition guidance (target language):

---
Swedish is a V2 language: the finite verb is the second constituent of a main clause, so fronting anything at all pushes the subject behind the verb. Write *I morgon åker vi till Malmö*, never *I morgon vi åker till Malmö*. This is the single most common structural tell of a text drafted in English and rendered into Swedish.

Compounds are written as one word. *Kvalitetssäkring*, *kundtjänstmedarbetare*, *miljökonsekvensbeskrivning*. Splitting them is not a stylistic choice in Swedish and often changes the meaning outright — *en rökfri miljö* and *en rök fri miljö* are different claims. Where a compound grows unreadably long, rewrite it into a prepositional phrase rather than splitting it.

Definiteness is marked twice. An adjective before a definite noun takes both the front article and the noun's suffix: *den nya rapporten*, *det stora huset*, *de svenska kunderna*. English has one article and drafts translated from it routinely lose one of the two Swedish markers.

The s-passive is the ordinary Swedish passive and is shorter than its periphrastic alternative: *rapporten skickas på fredag*, not *rapporten blir skickad på fredag*. Both exist; the s-form is the unmarked one, and the *bli*-form carries a change-of-state reading that is often not intended.

*Du* is the default address in Swedish prose, including business and journalism. *Ni* to a single reader is either archaic or a deliberate distancing, and reads as a translation from a language that has a formal pronoun.

*Man* is a fallback rather than the ordinary generic pronoun. It is justified where the agent genuinely is anybody at all or is genuinely unknown, and where naming one would claim more than the material carries. Where the sentence has a real subject to hand — the reader, the writer, the organisation, the profession, the study — that subject is what the sentence takes. A text that reaches for *man* with any of those available reads as evasive, and it is usually where an English draft's *you*, *we*, or passive has landed rather than anything the writer chose.

Speech that the text reports is ordinarily set with a speech dash rather than in quotation marks: an interview answer, a remark at a meeting, anything a person said that the text renders readable. A writer reaches for quotation marks where the phrasing itself is the point — where it is what is new, where it is disputed, or where the text is about how the thing was said. What each of the two marks promises a reader, and what that makes each of them a claim about, is settled in Mechanics; this scope says only which one an ordinary Swedish text reaches for first.

Genitive takes a bare *s* with no apostrophe: *Kntnts kunder*, *Sveriges riksdag*. A name already ending in *s*, *x*, or *z* takes nothing at all: *Anders bok*, *Marx teori*.

Swedish tolerates a shorter sentence than English does and punishes subordination harder. Prefer a main clause with a fronted adverbial to a long relative construction, and prefer a verb to a nominalisation: *när kommunen beslutade* over *vid kommunens beslutsfattande*.

Reach for the established Swedish term where one exists and the field actually uses it — *återkoppling*, *underlag*, *avstämning* — but do not purge the loanwords a professional reader expects. A text that writes *dator* and *webbplats* naturally is Swedish; a text that hunts down every English term and replaces it with a coinage nobody says is not.

Speech is not written prose, and a transcript quoted raw reads as carelessness towards the speaker rather than fidelity to them. So a spoken quotation may be repaired — cautiously, within a boundary that is easier to state than to feel your way to.

When translating permitted quotations, preserve meaning, stance, certainty and distinctive voice in idiomatic target-language speech, not source-language syntax. The restrictions below protect that substance; they do not require word-for-word translation. Make an implicit referent explicit only when the supplied context settles it. Where the meaning remains ambiguous, paraphrase what is established rather than inventing a fluent interpretation.

## What may be repaired

The syntax of speech: a sentence abandoned halfway and restarted, a subject left behind by its verb, a clause that never closes. Fillers — *you know*, *sort of*, *liksom*, *alltså* — where they carry nothing. Repetition that is the speaker searching for a word rather than insisting on one. False starts, and the small disfluencies a person does not hear themselves make.

That is the whole list. Everything on it is noise the speaker did not intend to produce, and removing it leaves what they meant to say.

## What may not

**Meaning.** Not narrowed, not widened, not sharpened. A speaker who said *most of them* has not said *all of them*, and one who said *we looked at it* has not said *we rejected it*.

**Stance.** Approval stays approval, reluctance stays reluctance, and a speaker who was careful not to blame anybody is not made to blame somebody by a tidier sentence.

**Certainty.** *I think*, *probably*, *as far as I know*, and *we are not sure yet* are the claim, not padding on it. Removing a hedge manufactures a confidence the speaker did not have; adding one takes away a confidence they did.

**Distinctive wording.** Where the speaker reached for an unusual word, an image, a piece of slang, or a phrasing that is theirs, it stays. Smoothing it into the register of the surrounding article is the most tempting of these failures and the one a reader can least detect.

**A self-correction.** Where a speaker gives a number or a fact and then corrects it, the correction is what they said. Quoting the first version is a misquotation; quoting a version that never existed — the correction with the correcting away — is worse.

**Anything additive.** Add no new meaning: no fact, stance, certainty, name, figure or connection that the speaker did not supply. A permitted repair or translation may change words only to render that same meaning.

## When to paraphrase instead

Where fidelity is uncertain, paraphrase. A paraphrase that attributes carefully — *she said the change had taken about a year, and that she was not sure it would hold* — is accurate, useful, and honest about what the material supports. A fluent direct quotation assembled out of a fragmentary answer is none of those things, however good it sounds.

The cases that should turn into paraphrase: material that is a summary of what somebody said rather than their words; a transcript too broken to repair inside the boundary above; several remarks that would have to be welded together to make one sentence; and any moment where you find yourself choosing between two readings of what the speaker meant.

Signal what the material actually is. Where the source is notes rather than a recording, the text says what the person said and does not pretend to their exact wording.

## What stays outside this

Whether the speaker approves the quotation. Quote approval is a human arrangement between the writer and the person quoted, and nothing here verifies it or stands in for it. A draft may say a quotation is unapproved; it may not treat the absence of approval as a problem it has solved.
---

Swedish composition guidance (target language):

---
Swedish is a V2 language: the finite verb is the second constituent of a main clause, so fronting anything at all pushes the subject behind the verb. Write *I morgon åker vi till Malmö*, never *I morgon vi åker till Malmö*. This is the single most common structural tell of a text drafted in English and rendered into Swedish.

Compounds are written as one word. *Kvalitetssäkring*, *kundtjänstmedarbetare*, *miljökonsekvensbeskrivning*. Splitting them is not a stylistic choice in Swedish and often changes the meaning outright — *en rökfri miljö* and *en rök fri miljö* are different claims. Where a compound grows unreadably long, rewrite it into a prepositional phrase rather than splitting it.

Definiteness is marked twice. An adjective before a definite noun takes both the front article and the noun's suffix: *den nya rapporten*, *det stora huset*, *de svenska kunderna*. English has one article and drafts translated from it routinely lose one of the two Swedish markers.

The s-passive is the ordinary Swedish passive and is shorter than its periphrastic alternative: *rapporten skickas på fredag*, not *rapporten blir skickad på fredag*. Both exist; the s-form is the unmarked one, and the *bli*-form carries a change-of-state reading that is often not intended.

*Du* is the default address in Swedish prose, including business and journalism. *Ni* to a single reader is either archaic or a deliberate distancing, and reads as a translation from a language that has a formal pronoun.

*Man* is a fallback rather than the ordinary generic pronoun. It is justified where the agent genuinely is anybody at all or is genuinely unknown, and where naming one would claim more than the material carries. Where the sentence has a real subject to hand — the reader, the writer, the organisation, the profession, the study — that subject is what the sentence takes. A text that reaches for *man* with any of those available reads as evasive, and it is usually where an English draft's *you*, *we*, or passive has landed rather than anything the writer chose.

Speech that the text reports is ordinarily set with a speech dash rather than in quotation marks: an interview answer, a remark at a meeting, anything a person said that the text renders readable. A writer reaches for quotation marks where the phrasing itself is the point — where it is what is new, where it is disputed, or where the text is about how the thing was said. What each of the two marks promises a reader, and what that makes each of them a claim about, is settled in Mechanics; this scope says only which one an ordinary Swedish text reaches for first.

Genitive takes a bare *s* with no apostrophe: *Kntnts kunder*, *Sveriges riksdag*. A name already ending in *s*, *x*, or *z* takes nothing at all: *Anders bok*, *Marx teori*.

Swedish tolerates a shorter sentence than English does and punishes subordination harder. Prefer a main clause with a fronted adverbial to a long relative construction, and prefer a verb to a nominalisation: *när kommunen beslutade* over *vid kommunens beslutsfattande*.

Reach for the established Swedish term where one exists and the field actually uses it — *återkoppling*, *underlag*, *avstämning* — but do not purge the loanwords a professional reader expects. A text that writes *dator* and *webbplats* naturally is Swedish; a text that hunts down every English term and replaces it with a coinage nobody says is not.

# Claim-support report: Elm Quay case (sv draft vs English material)

Scope: source support and translation of quotations only. General editorial and mechanical review are excluded. Byline and frontmatter are not assessed as claims (per instructions).

## 1. Claim accounting

Each row pairs a draft passage (D) with the source passage (S) it rests on, in the source's own words, and then states what differs.

**Title (l. 8).** D: "Elm Quays arbetsledare skulle göra om provet"
S: "maintenance supervisor Maya Lind" / "I would choose to do the trial again."
Differences: (a) "välja" (choose) is dropped. "göra om provet" has a strong Swedish collocation of retaking a failed test, so it can read as "would have to redo / would redo differently" and not as a voluntary, positive choice. See finding S3. (b) The definite genitive "Elm Quays arbetsledare" presents Lind as the company's (unique) supervisor. The source says only "maintenance supervisor", and nothing excludes other supervisors, for example on other shifts. Also finding S3.

**Standfirst (l. 10), sentence 1.** D: "Underhållsteamet på bostadsbolaget Elm Quay Housing provade under åtta veckor en delad reparationslogg från Svale Systems i två hus."
S: "its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings" / "It chose Svale Systems" / "The trial lasted eight weeks."
No material difference. "bostadsbolaget" rests on the brief ("small housing companies"; "Lind did not recommend Svale to every housing company"). "hus" = buildings.

**Standfirst, sentence 2.** D: "Här är vad provet krävde, vad siffrorna säger och inte säger och hur arbetsledaren Maya Lind ser på förberedelserna inför nästa hus."
S: "I would set that time aside before the next building starts." / "The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs."
Difference: Lind's conditional remark ("I would … before the next building starts") becomes a narrator presupposition that there is a next building. See finding S1. The rest ("vad provet krävde", "vad siffrorna säger och inte säger") is editorial framing that rests on supported material.

**l. 14.** D: "Telefonanmälningar och mejl sparades tidigare var för sig hos Elm Quay Housing, som förvaltar 640 lägenheter."
S: "Previously telephone reports and emails were stored separately." / "Elm Quay Housing manages 640 flats."
No difference.

D: "I september 2025 beslutade bolagets eget underhållsteam att pröva en gemensam reparationslogg i två hus."
S: "In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings."
No difference.

D: "En intern provanteckning och arbetsledaren Maya Lind ger var sin bild av hur det gick."
S: "Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025 …" / "Customer interview with maintenance supervisor Maya Lind".
This is an authorial transition resting on supported material. No finding. "arbetsledaren" for "maintenance supervisor" is adequate in context, because the preceding sentence names the maintenance team.

**H2 (l. 16).** D: "Teamet valde Svale efter ett test av loggen"
S: "It chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair."
No difference.

**Quote 1 (l. 18).** D: "– Vi ville att kvällsskiftet skulle se vad morgonskiftet redan hade gjort. Kategorierna var våra. Svale hjälpte oss att lägga in dem i loggen, skriver Lind i ett mejlsvar."
S: "We wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done. The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log." / "All interviews occurred by email".
The translation is faithful and idiomatic, and the stance (ownership of the categories, Svale in a helping role) is preserved. "skriver … i ett mejlsvar" correctly signals an email answer.

**l. 20.** D: "Testet gällde om loggen kunde visa status för varje reparation. Någon jämförelse med en annan leverantör finns inte att tillgå."
S: "after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair. No comparison with another supplier is available."
No difference. The same epistemic status ("available") is kept.

**l. 22.** D: "Svale Systems konfigurerade loggen och utbildade sex medarbetare vid två tillfällen."
S: "Svale configured the log and trained six staff during two sessions."
No difference.

D: "Teamet lät samtidigt de boende fortsätta att anmäla fel per telefon."
S: "The maintenance team … kept telephone reporting open for residents."
"samtidigt" adds a loose simultaneity. "kept … open" is continuous, so no case can be named in which the source holds and the draft fails. No finding.

**H2 (l. 24).** D: "Mediantiden till tilldelning sjönk – programvaran pekas inte ut"
S: "Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period. The periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software."
"sjönk" is a descriptive comparison (3 to 2) and makes no causal claim. The agentless "pekas inte ut" widens whose position this is, from the note's to no one's. See finding S4.

**l. 26.** D: "Provet pågick i åtta veckor."
S: "The trial lasted eight weeks."
No difference.

D: "Enligt Elm Quays interna provanteckning från den 4 december 2025 fördes 31 felanmälningar in i loggen."
S: "Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered."
No difference. "i loggen" is settled by context, and "felanmälningar" names the reports that are later assigned.

D: "Akuta ärenden och arbeten som beställts före provet är inte medräknade."
S: "It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial."
Difference in scope: the source's subject is the note ("It"), so the exclusion governs the note's figures, including the trial median. The draft ties the exclusion to the count alone. See finding S2.

**l. 28.** D: "Från anmälan till tilldelning tog det i median två arbetsdagar under provet, mot tre under de åtta veckorna dessförinnan."
S: "Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period."
The figures, unit, measure (assignment, not completion) and periods match. The note's exclusions are not carried over (S2).

D: "Arbetsbelastningen skilde sig mellan perioderna, och anteckningen tillskriver uttryckligen inte skillnaden programvaran."
S: "The periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software."
No difference.

**l. 30.** D: "Mätningar av kostnader, de boendes nöjdhet eller tiden tills reparationerna var klara finns inte."
S: "There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements."
No difference.

**H2 (l. 32).** D: "Arbetsledaren ser tillbaka på provet"
Framing only. No finding.

**Quote 2 (l. 34).** D: "– Vi lade mer tid på att komma överens om kategorierna än på att föra in de första anmälningarna. Den tiden skulle jag avsätta innan det är dags för nästa hus, skriver Lind."
S: "We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts."
Faithful. The conditional "skulle" is kept, and the idiom is natural.

**Quote 3 (l. 36).** D: "– Jag skulle välja att göra provet igen. Att se anmälningarna på ett ställe hjälper oss, men jag skulle ge förberedelserna en vecka till."
S: "I would choose to do the trial again. Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation."
The stance, the "but" reservation and the conditional are all kept. However, "one view" becomes "på ett ställe" (in one place). See translation finding T1. The attribution carries over from the preceding "skriver Lind", which is acceptable.

**l. 38.** D: "Någon rekommendation av Svale till alla bostadsbolag ger Lind inte."
S: "Lind did not recommend Svale to every housing company."
Difference: "rekommendation av Svale" is ambiguous in Swedish between "a recommendation of Svale" and "a recommendation by Svale". See finding S5. The not-all scope is otherwise preserved.

**H2 (l. 40) and l. 42.** D: "Frågan om att vidga provet är ännu öppen" / "Hittills har provet bara gällt de två husen. Teamet tar ställning när det har sett hur kategorierna fungerar för större reparationer."
S: "The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs."
No difference.

**CTA (l. 44).** D: "Planerar du ett liknande prov kan du läsa [checklistan för införandet](https://example.invalid/svale/checklist)."
S: "the supplied implementation checklist at https://example.invalid/svale/checklist; it is a document to read, not a consultation booking or a product trial."
The link accurately describes its destination as a document to read. No finding.

### Pronoun accounting (person, number, natural gender)

- "Vi" (l. 18, l. 34) and "oss" (l. 18, l. 36): first person plural, from the source's "We"/"us". They match.
- "dem" (l. 18): third person plural, referring to "kategorierna", from the source's "them". It matches, and it carries no gender.
- "jag" (l. 34, l. 36): first person singular, from the source's "I". It matches.
- "det" (l. 42, "när det har sett"): third person singular, grammatical neuter agreeing with "teamet". It is purely grammatical and makes no natural-gender assertion. It matches the source's "the team" (singular).
- "du" (l. 44): second person singular addressing the reader. This is the author's own address, not a claim.
- Lind is never referred to with "hon" or "han". The draft asserts no natural gender, and the source supplies no pronoun for her. There is no finding.

## 2. Findings: source support

**S1. Standfirst presupposes a next building (modality/certainty).**
- Draft (l. 10): "hur arbetsledaren Maya Lind ser på förberedelserna inför nästa hus."
- Source: "I would set that time aside before the next building starts." / "The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs."
- What differs: Lind's conditional remark becomes a narrator-voice presupposition that another building will follow.
- Case: the team checks the categories and decides not to expand. Every source statement still holds, but the draft's "förberedelserna inför nästa hus" refers to a stage that never comes. No supplied statement excludes this case.
- Smallest repair: "… ser på förberedelserna inför ett eventuellt nästa hus."

**S2. The note's exclusions are narrowed to the count (scope).**
- Draft (l. 26): "Akuta ärenden och arbeten som beställts före provet är inte medräknade." The median follows on l. 28 without that qualification.
- Source: "Elm Quay's internal trial note … says that 31 repair reports were entered. It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial."
- What differs: the source's exclusion has the note as its subject and so applies across the note's figures. The draft attaches it to the count only, which leaves the trial median reading as though it covered all repairs in the trial.
- Case: emergencies were assigned the same day but are left out of the note's median. A reader of the draft takes "i median två arbetsdagar under provet" to include them, which is a statement the source does not make.
- Smallest repair, restoring the source's scope: "Anteckningen räknar inte med akuta ärenden och arbeten som beställts före provet."

**S3. The title changes stance and scope.**
- Draft (l. 8): "Elm Quays arbetsledare skulle göra om provet"
- Source: "I would choose to do the trial again." / "maintenance supervisor Maya Lind"
- What differs:
  - (a) With "välja" dropped, "göra om provet" carries the common Swedish reading of retaking or redoing a test that failed or has to be done differently. The source is a voluntary, positive choice, which the source calls "her actual, qualified assessment".
  - (b) The definite genitive implies that Lind is Elm Quay's supervisor. The source says only that she is a maintenance supervisor.
- Cases:
  - (a) A reader takes the title to mean that the trial went wrong and would need redoing. Nothing in the source supports that.
  - (b) Elm Quay has more than one supervisor, for example on the morning and evening shifts. The title's uniqueness then fails, and nothing supplied excludes this.
- Smallest repair: "Arbetsledare på Elm Quay skulle välja att göra provet igen".

**S4. The heading leaves open whose non-attribution this is (whose assertion).** Low severity.
- Draft (l. 24): "– programvaran pekas inte ut"
- Source: "the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software."
- What differs: the agentless passive states that nobody singles out the software. The source reports only the note's position.
- Case: another party, such as the supplier's own material, attributes the drop to the software. The source still holds and the heading fails. No supplied statement excludes this.
- Smallest repair: "Mediantiden till tilldelning sjönk – anteckningen pekar inte ut programvaran".

**S5. "rekommendation av Svale" can read as Svale's own recommendation (meaning in translation).** Low severity.
- Draft (l. 38): "Någon rekommendation av Svale till alla bostadsbolag ger Lind inte."
- Source: "Lind did not recommend Svale to every housing company."
- What differs: in Swedish, "rekommendation av X" ordinarily reads as a recommendation issued by X, so the sentence can be parsed as Lind not passing on a recommendation made by Svale. The source means that Lind did not recommend Svale.
- Smallest repair, which also keeps the act reading (she did not make such a recommendation) rather than stating a negative position: "Lind rekommenderade inte Svale till alla bostadsbolag."

## 3. Findings: translation of quotations

**T1. "one view" becomes "på ett ställe".**
- Draft (l. 36): "Att se anmälningarna på ett ställe hjälper oss"
- Source: "Having one view of the reports helps us"
- What differs: "one view" is Lind's wording. It covers a single consolidated view that everyone sees, which fits the team's goal that "staff on different shifts … see the same information". "på ett ställe" narrows this to storage location.
- Case: the reports sit in one place but each shift uses a different view. The draft's quotation then holds while Lind's does not.
- Smallest repair: "Att ha en samlad vy över anmälningarna hjälper oss".

There are no other translation findings. Quotes 1 and 2 and the remainder of quote 3 keep their meaning, stance, conditionals and reservation in idiomatic Swedish.

## 4. Editorial question (not a defect)

The material states: "The supplier approved publication of this case as supplier-published material; it is not independent journalism." The draft does not say that it is supplier-published, and it does not claim independence either. Whether a disclosure line is needed depends on the publication context: the brief says Svale is the publisher. This is left to the editor.

## Completion status

Complete. All factual and attributed claims in the title, standfirst, headings, body, quotations and call to action have been accounted for. Unresolved findings: S1, S2, S3, S4 (low) and S5 (low) on source support; T1 on translation. There is one editorial question (disclosure of supplier publication).

**Meaning.** Not narrowed, not widened, not sharpened. A speaker who said *most of them* has not said *all of them*, and one who said *we looked at it* has not said *we rejected it*.

**Stance.** Approval stays approval, reluctance stays reluctance, and a speaker who was careful not to blame anybody is not made to blame somebody by a tidier sentence.

**Certainty.** *I think*, *probably*, *as far as I know*, and *we are not sure yet* are the claim, not padding on it. Removing a hedge manufactures a confidence the speaker did not have; adding one takes away a confidence they did.

**Distinctive wording.** Where the speaker reached for an unusual word, an image, a piece of slang, or a phrasing that is theirs, it stays. Smoothing it into the register of the surrounding article is the most tempting of these failures and the one a reader can least detect.

**A self-correction.** Where a speaker gives a number or a fact and then corrects it, the correction is what they said. Quoting the first version is a misquotation; quoting a version that never existed — the correction with the correcting away — is worse.

**Anything additive.** Add no new meaning: no fact, stance, certainty, name, figure or connection that the speaker did not supply. A permitted repair or translation may change words only to render that same meaning.

## When to paraphrase instead

Where fidelity is uncertain, paraphrase. A paraphrase that attributes carefully — *she said the change had taken about a year, and that she was not sure it would hold* — is accurate, useful, and honest about what the material supports. A fluent direct quotation assembled out of a fragmentary answer is none of those things, however good it sounds.

The cases that should turn into paraphrase: material that is a summary of what somebody said rather than their words; a transcript too broken to repair inside the boundary above; several remarks that would have to be welded together to make one sentence; and any moment where you find yourself choosing between two readings of what the speaker meant.

Signal what the material actually is. Where the source is notes rather than a recording, the text says what the person said and does not pretend to their exact wording.

## What stays outside this

Whether the speaker approves the quotation. Quote approval is a human arrangement between the writer and the person quoted, and nothing here verifies it or stands in for it. A draft may say a quotation is unapproved; it may not treat the absence of approval as a problem it has solved.
---

Swedish composition guidance (target language):

---
Swedish is a V2 language: the finite verb is the second constituent of a main clause, so fronting anything at all pushes the subject behind the verb. Write *I morgon åker vi till Malmö*, never *I morgon vi åker till Malmö*. This is the single most common structural tell of a text drafted in English and rendered into Swedish.

Compounds are written as one word. *Kvalitetssäkring*, *kundtjänstmedarbetare*, *miljökonsekvensbeskrivning*. Splitting them is not a stylistic choice in Swedish and often changes the meaning outright — *en rökfri miljö* and *en rök fri miljö* are different claims. Where a compound grows unreadably long, rewrite it into a prepositional phrase rather than splitting it.

Definiteness is marked twice. An adjective before a definite noun takes both the front article and the noun's suffix: *den nya rapporten*, *det stora huset*, *de svenska kunderna*. English has one article and drafts translated from it routinely lose one of the two Swedish markers.

The s-passive is the ordinary Swedish passive and is shorter than its periphrastic alternative: *rapporten skickas på fredag*, not *rapporten blir skickad på fredag*. Both exist; the s-form is the unmarked one, and the *bli*-form carries a change-of-state reading that is often not intended.

*Du* is the default address in Swedish prose, including business and journalism. *Ni* to a single reader is either archaic or a deliberate distancing, and reads as a translation from a language that has a formal pronoun.

*Man* is a fallback rather than the ordinary generic pronoun. It is justified where the agent genuinely is anybody at all or is genuinely unknown, and where naming one would claim more than the material carries. Where the sentence has a real subject to hand — the reader, the writer, the organisation, the profession, the study — that subject is what the sentence takes. A text that reaches for *man* with any of those available reads as evasive, and it is usually where an English draft's *you*, *we*, or passive has landed rather than anything the writer chose.

Speech that the text reports is ordinarily set with a speech dash rather than in quotation marks: an interview answer, a remark at a meeting, anything a person said that the text renders readable. A writer reaches for quotation marks where the phrasing itself is the point — where it is what is new, where it is disputed, or where the text is about how the thing was said. What each of the two marks promises a reader, and what that makes each of them a claim about, is settled in Mechanics; this scope says only which one an ordinary Swedish text reaches for first.

Genitive takes a bare *s* with no apostrophe: *Kntnts kunder*, *Sveriges riksdag*. A name already ending in *s*, *x*, or *z* takes nothing at all: *Anders bok*, *Marx teori*.

Swedish tolerates a shorter sentence than English does and punishes subordination harder. Prefer a main clause with a fronted adverbial to a long relative construction, and prefer a verb to a nominalisation: *när kommunen beslutade* over *vid kommunens beslutsfattande*.

Reach for the established Swedish term where one exists and the field actually uses it — *återkoppling*, *underlag*, *avstämning* — but do not purge the loanwords a professional reader expects. A text that writes *dator* and *webbplats* naturally is Swedish; a text that hunts down every English term and replaces it with a coinage nobody says is not.
---

Distinguish natural-gender assertions from purely grammatical gender. For each pair, state what differs: the thing named or measured, the subject, scope, time, modality, certainty, or whose knowledge or assertion it is. A term carried into another language names the same thing only where nothing in this context could fall under one term and not the other. Where the two differ, test both directions: name a concrete case, compatible with the supplied material, in which one statement holds and the other fails. The case need only be compatible with the supplied material; the material need not describe it or make it likely. Set a case aside only by quoting a supplied statement that excludes it. If a case stands, that is a finding, however natural or cautious the draft’s wording; if you can name none, it is not. Read such a passage as an ordinary reader would in its context, and test the facts, events, experiences and views it presents as given, not the reasoning or transition itself. That the brief establishes who asserts something establishes nothing about whether it is so. # Claim accounting: Elm Quay case draft (sv) against source (en)

Scope: I compared every factual and attributed claim in the draft (title, lead, body, headings, quotations and link text) with /work/source.md. Frontmatter and byline are out of scope, as instructed. General editorial and mechanical review is also out of scope.

## 1. Claim-by-claim accounting

| # | Draft passage | Source passage (source wording) | What differs / test | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Title: "Elm Quay fick en samlad bild av felanmälningarna" | Lind: "Having one view of the reports helps us"; "In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings."; "31 repair reports were entered. It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial." | Subject: the draft names Elm Quay (the whole company, "manages 640 flats"), but the source covers a trial in two buildings. Scope: definite "felanmälningarna" means all reports. Whose assertion: the source has Lind's own view ("helps us"), and the draft states it as narrator fact. Case: reports from Elm Quay's other buildings, and possibly emergencies (excluded from the note), were not in the log. Elm Quay as a company therefore did not get a unified view of its fault reports, although the two-building trial did. No supplied statement rules this out. | **Finding S1** |
| 2 | Lead: "Underhållsteamet på bostadsbolaget Elm Quay Housing provade under åtta veckor en delad reparationslogg från Svale Systems i två hus." | "its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings"; "It chose Svale Systems"; "The trial lasted eight weeks." | Same subject, scope, time and object. | Supported |
| 3 | Lead: "vad arbetsledaren Maya Lind skulle göra annorlunda inför nästa hus" | "maintenance supervisor Maya Lind"; "I would set that time aside before the next building starts."; "I would leave an extra week for preparation." | Conditional "skulle" matches her "would". "arbetsledaren" is less specific than "maintenance supervisor" but says nothing false. | Supported |
| 4 | "Telefonanmälningar och mejl sparades tidigare var för sig hos Elm Quay Housing, som förvaltar 640 lägenheter." | "Elm Quay Housing manages 640 flats."; "Previously telephone reports and emails were stored separately." | Same. The draft keeps the source's ambiguity about "emails". | Supported |
| 5 | "I september 2025 beslutade bolagets eget underhållsteam att pröva en gemensam reparationslogg i två hus." | "In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings." | Same. | Supported |
| 6 | "En intern provanteckning och arbetsledaren Maya Lind ger var sin bild av hur det gick." | Internal trial note of 4 December 2025; "Customer interview with maintenance supervisor Maya Lind" | This is framing. "var sin" means "each their own" and does not claim that the two accounts disagree. | Supported |
| 7 | Heading: "Svale valdes efter ett test av loggen" | "It chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair." | The passive drops the agent but claims nothing false. The sequence is the same. | Supported |
| 8 | "– Vi ville att kvällsskiftet … lägga in dem i loggen, skriver Lind i ett mejlsvar." | Quotation 1; "All interviews occurred by email" | "skriver … i ett mejlsvar" correctly signals written email answers. For the translation, see section 3. | Supported |
| 9 | "Innan beslutet prövade underhållsteamet om loggen kunde visa status för varje reparation." | "It chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair." | The test itself matches. Chronology: "beslutet" has no stated referent. The only decision the draft has named so far is "beslutade … att pröva en gemensam reparationslogg" (September 2025), so "beslutet" can be read as the decision to run a trial at all. Case: in September the team decides to trial a shared log, then tests Svale's log and chooses Svale. The source's order holds (test before choice). The draft's reading "test before the decision to trial" fails. No supplied statement orders the test relative to the September decision. | **Finding S2** |
| 10 | "Någon jämförelse med en annan leverantör finns inte att tillgå." | "No comparison with another supplier is available." | Same knowledge state: not available, and not "none was made". | Supported |
| 11 | "Svale Systems konfigurerade loggen och utbildade sex medarbetare vid två tillfällen." | "Svale configured the log and trained six staff during two sessions." | Same. | Supported |
| 12 | "Teamet lät samtidigt de boende fortsätta att anmäla fel per telefon." | "The maintenance team … kept telephone reporting open for residents." | "fortsätta" matches "kept … open". "samtidigt": the phone line was kept open (never closed), so it was open while Svale configured and trained. I found no case where the draft holds and the source fails. | Supported |
| 13 | Heading: "Mediantiden till tilldelning sjönk – programvaran pekas inte ut" | "Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period. … the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software." | "sjönk" compares the two periods and has no causal agent. The heading keeps the non-attribution. It concerns assignment, not completion. | Supported |
| 14 | "Provet pågick i åtta veckor. Enligt Elm Quays interna provanteckning från den 4 december 2025 fördes 31 felanmälningar in i loggen." | "The trial lasted eight weeks. Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered." | "i loggen" makes explicit what the context settles (a trial of the log). Attribution to the note is kept. "felanmälningar"/"repair reports": both are reports of something needing repair. I could not name a report that falls under one term and not the other in this context. | Supported |
| 15 | "Akuta ärenden och arbeten som beställts före provet är inte medräknade." | "It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial." | Same exclusions. The source attaches them to the note as a whole, and the draft's general "är inte medräknade" does not narrow that. | Supported |
| 16 | "Från anmälan till tilldelning tog det i median två arbetsdagar under provet, mot tre under de åtta veckorna dessförinnan." | Median sentence (see #13) | Same measure, units and periods. | Supported |
| 17 | "Arbetsbelastningen skilde sig mellan perioderna, och anteckningen tillskriver uttryckligen inte skillnaden programvaran." | "The periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software." | Same, including "explicitly". | Supported |
| 18 | "Mätningar av kostnader, de boendes nöjdhet eller tiden tills reparationerna var klara finns inte." | "There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements." | Same. | Supported |
| 19 | Heading: "Arbetsledaren ser tillbaka på provet" | Lind's quotations 2 and 3 | This is framing, and it is supported. | Supported |
| 20 | "– Vi lade mer tid … inför/innan det är dags för nästa hus, skriver Lind." | Quotation 2 | For the translation, see section 3. | Supported |
| 21 | "– Jag skulle välja att göra provet igen. … en vecka till." | Quotation 3 | This continues the Lind attribution from #20. For the translation, see section 3. | Supported |
| 22 | "Någon rekommendation av Svale till alla bostadsbolag ger Lind inte." | "Lind did not recommend Svale to every housing company." | Same scope (a blanket recommendation is withheld). It does not claim she recommends nobody. The present tense "ger" is ordinary reporting present for a statement given in the interview. | Supported |
| 23 | Heading: "Utvidgningen väntar på erfarenheter från större reparationer" | "The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs." | Modality: the definite "Utvidgningen" presupposes that an expansion will happen and is only delayed. The source says the decision is still open. Scope: the source makes the decision depend on how *the categories* work for larger repairs, while the heading says "experiences from larger repairs" in general. Case: the team checks the categories on larger repairs and decides not to expand. The source holds, and the heading ("the expansion is waiting") fails. No supplied statement says an expansion will follow. | **Finding S3** |
| 24 | "Än så länge har provet inte vidgats utöver de två husen." | "The trial has not yet expanded" | "utöver de två husen" makes explicit what the two-building scope settles. | Supported |
| 25 | "Teamet fattar beslut när det har sett hur kategorierna fungerar för större reparationer." | "the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs." | Same. | Supported |
| 26 | "Planerar du ett liknande prov kan du läsa [checklistan för införandet](https://example.invalid/svale/checklist)." | Brief: "the supplied implementation checklist … it is a document to read, not a consultation booking or a product trial." | The link describes a document to read. It does not claim the checklist was written for trials. | Supported |

Not claimed by the draft, so not tested as claims: savings, resident satisfaction, completion time, causal effect of the software, rescue narrative, physical scene or emotion. The draft makes no claim to independence. Whether to disclose supplier publication is an editorial matter outside this comparison.

## 2. Pronoun accounting (person, number, natural gender)

- "du" (CTA, #26): second person singular, addressing the reader. The brief's audience is operations managers, so this is generic address. No natural gender.
- "Vi", "oss", "våra" (quotations 1–3): first person plural, the same as the source's "We", "us", "ours". The number is kept.
- "jag" (quotations 2–3): first person singular, the same as the source's "I". The draft adds no gender.
- "dem" (quotation 1): third person plural, referring to "Kategorierna". This matches the source's "them". No natural gender.
- "det" (#25, "när det har sett"): third person singular with neuter grammatical gender, referring to "Teamet". This is purely grammatical and asserts no natural gender.
- "bolagets eget" (#5): possessive for Elm Quay, the same as the source's "its own". Grammatical only.
- The draft has no "hon" or "han". The source's "Her final quotation" shows Lind as female, and the draft does not assert her gender. Nothing is added or contradicted.

## 3. Translated quotations (translation check)

- Q1: "We wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done. The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log." → "Vi ville att kvällsskiftet skulle se vad morgonskiftet redan hade gjort. Kategorierna var våra. Svale hjälpte oss att lägga in dem i loggen." The meaning, the ownership stance ("var våra") and Svale's supporting role are kept. Splitting at the semicolon is harmless. No obstruction.
- Q2: "We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts." → "Vi lade mer tid på att komma överens om kategorierna än på att föra in de första anmälningarna. Den tiden skulle jag avsätta innan det är dags för nästa hus." The comparison, the conditional advice and the reference to the next building are kept. The Swedish is idiomatic and V2 is correct. No obstruction.
- Q3: "I would choose to do the trial again. Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation." → "Jag skulle välja att göra provet igen. Att se anmälningarna på ett ställe hjälper oss, men jag skulle ge förberedelserna en vecka till." "One view" is rendered as "se … på ett ställe", which is the same meaning in natural Swedish. Her reservation ("men … en vecka till") and the conditional stance are kept. No obstruction.

Translation findings: none.

## 4. Findings

### Source-support findings

**S1: The title widens a two-building trial and Lind's own view into a company-wide fact** (line 8)
- Draft: "Elm Quay fick en samlad bild av felanmälningarna"
- Source: "decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings"; Lind: "Having one view of the reports helps us"; the note "excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial."
- What changed: the subject (the company instead of the two-building trial), the scope (all fault reports) and whose assertion it is (narrator instead of Lind). Case: reports from buildings outside the trial were not in the log, so the title's statement fails while the source holds.
- Smallest repair: limit the scope to the trial, e.g. "Elm Quay provade en samlad bild av felanmälningarna i två hus". Alternatively, attribute it: "'Att se anmälningarna på ett ställe hjälper oss'".

**S2: "Innan beslutet" can place the test before the September decision to trial a log** (line 20)
- Draft: "Innan beslutet prövade underhållsteamet om loggen kunde visa status för varje reparation."
- Source: "It chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair."
- What changed: chronology, through an unanchored referent. The only decision named earlier in the draft is the September decision "att pröva en gemensam reparationslogg". The source orders the test only relative to choosing Svale.
- Smallest repair: "Innan teamet valde Svale prövade det om loggen kunde visa status för varje reparation."

**S3: The heading presupposes an expansion the source leaves undecided** (line 40)
- Draft: "Utvidgningen väntar på erfarenheter från större reparationer"
- Source: "The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs."
- What changed: modality (the definite "Utvidgningen" presents an open decision as a delayed certainty) and scope (the categories on larger repairs become larger repairs in general). Case: the team decides not to expand after checking.
- Smallest repair: "Beslut om utvidgning väntar på hur kategorierna fungerar för större reparationer".

### Translation findings
None.

## 5. Completion status

Complete. All claims in the title, lead, headings, body, quotations and link text have been accounted for. Three source-support findings (S1, S2, S3) are unresolved in the draft and need repair. There are no translation findings. No editorial questions remain open.
